message.content:
**Answer:**  
One of the most iconic and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” by Auguste Rodin (1889)**.  

**Why it’s so famous:**  
- It captures a tender, almost erotic moment between two lovers, which was daring for its time.  
- Rodin’s treatment of flesh, drapery, and movement was revolutionary, influencing modern sculpture.  
- The work has been reproduced, parodied, and referenced countless times in popular culture, making it instantly recognizable even to people who have never seen the original marble.

**Other contenders for “most famous” in the same era:**  
| Sculpture | Artist | Year | Why it matters |
|-----------|--------|------|----------------|
| **“The Burghers of Calais”** | Auguste Rodin | 1889 | A powerful civic monument that showcases Rodin’s mastery of emotion and form. |
| **“The Gates of Hell”** | Auguste Rodin | 1880‑1917 | An ambitious, unfinished monumental work that became a cornerstone of modern sculpture. |
| **“The Rape of the Sabine Women”** | Jean‑Baptiste Regnault | 1858 | A dramatic, narrative piece that exemplifies 19th‑century French academic sculpture. |
| **“The Death of Sardanapalus”** | Jean‑Baptiste Regnault | 1855 | A grand, theatrical composition that was celebrated at the Paris Salon. |

While many of these works are highly regarded, **“The Kiss”** is arguably the most universally known and frequently cited example of 19th‑century sculpture.
